_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: No Man's Sky contains 18 quintillion planets.
beats.note: A quintillion is a billion billion. The number is not an exaggeration; it is arithmetic.

beats.context: 2 to the power of 64, the exact count of values a 64-bit seed number can take. Every planet in the game traces back to one number in that range.

beats.lead: Here is the part people get backwards
beats.text: Every player explores the same universe.
beats.note: Not a private, randomly generated world each time; one shared seed, unpacked locally, so two players who visit the same coordinates find the same planet.

beats.name: Hello Games
beats.role: A 13-person studio in the UK. Art director Grant Duncan described the process as running seed values through what he called 'boxes of math'.

beats.text: The universe was not built by hand. It was built by one number, run through the right equations.

beats.line: Infinite was never the hard part. Consistent was.
